facts.claim: The Sun contains 99.86% of the total mass of the Solar System.
The Sun's core temperature is approximately 15 million degrees Celsius.
The Sun's surface temperature is about 5,500 degrees Celsius.
The Sun is approximately 4.6 billion years old.
The Sun is about 93 million miles (150 million kilometers) from Earth.
The Sun's diameter is about 1.39 million kilometers.
The Sun's mass is about 1.989 × 10^30 kilograms.
The Sun's energy output is about 3.8 × 10^26 watts.
The Sun converts about 600 million tons of hydrogen into helium per second.
The Sun's magnetic field reverses polarity approximately every 11 years during the solar cycle.
The Parker Solar Probe, launched in 2018, became the closest human-made object to the Sun, coming within 6.1 million kilometers of the surface in 2024.
The Sun is currently in its main sequence phase and will remain there for about 5 billion more years.
The Sun's corona is hotter than its surface, with temperatures exceeding 1 million degrees Celsius.
The Sun's rotation period at its equator is about 25 days, while at its poles it takes about 35 days.

hook_ideas: What if the Sun suddenly stopped shining? (The darkness would take 8 minutes to reach us, but we'd freeze within days.)
The Sun is 330,000 times heavier than Earth — yet it's just an average star.
We're all made of star dust — the Sun's energy powers every life on Earth, but a single solar flare can disrupt our tech.
How do we know the Sun's age? From meteorites, not the Sun itself.
misconceptions: The Sun is not burning (combustion) — it's fuse hydrogen into helium via nuclear fusion.
The Sun is not yellow — it appears yellow from Earth due to atmospheric scattering; its true color is white.
The Sun does not rise and set — Earth rotates; the Sun is stationary relative to the Earth's orbit.
The Sun is not a solid object — it's a glowing ball of plasma.
